turns.content: Okay so I'm annoyed haha. My direct deposit for that $85 cat-sitting gig hasn't processed in four days and I lowkey worry Chloe is punishing me because I submitted the wrong voided check form at first... which I know is probably paranoid but ugh. Anyway could you just draft me a quick friendly two-sentence text to her just checking on the status? Nothing formal or confrontational, I refuse to make this a thing over side cash.

Ha, I feel this — the "did I screw this up forever" spiral is so real, but four days is actually pretty normal for a first-time direct deposit setup, especially with a corrected form in the mix. Here's a text:

"Hey Chloe! Just checking in — my direct deposit for the cat-sitting gig hasn't hit yet, could you let me know when it processed on your end? No rush at all, just want to make sure the new check form went through okay 🙂"

Short, casual, and it subtly confirms the corrected form landed without making it A Thing.

Hmm okay that's actually a really good point about four days being normal for a first setup haha. I guess I'm just overthinking it because of the wrong form thing.

Think I should send it now or wait until Monday morning?

I'd wait until Monday morning, and here's why: today is Saturday, and banks don't process ACH transfers over the weekend anyway — so even if the deposit went out, nothing would move until Monday. Sending a "where's my money?" text on a weekend when literally nothing could have happened is the one move that would make it A Thing.

Also, practical bonus: if it was submitted mid-week, there's a decent chance it just shows up Monday or Tuesday on its own and you never have to send the text at all. Give it until Monday morning, and if nothing's hit by then, send it around 9-10am when Chloe's actually at her desk and can check on it.

Your paranoia about the wrong form is understandable, but honestly — people submit wrong voided checks constantly. It's a fixable paperwork hiccup, not a punishable offense. 😄

Yeah okay you're so right about not sending it on a weekend haha. That would def make it A Thing. I'll hold off til Monday morning ✨

But ugh now I'm spiraling a little like... what if she *is* annoyed about the wrong form and that's why it's taking long?? Like am I being paranoid??

Okay deep breath — you're being a *little* paranoid, and I say that with love. 😄

Here's the thing: think about what "punishing you over a voided check" would actually require on Chloe's end. She'd have to see the wrong form, feel genuinely annoyed by a super common mistake, and then deliberately sit on your $85 out of spite... for a cat-sitting gig. That's a lot of petty energy for side cash. Most people's reaction to a wrong form is "huh, wrong form" → resubmit → forget it happened by lunch.

The boring truth is almost always the real one: first-time direct deposits take 3-5 business days, you resubmitted a form which probably restarted part of the process, and a weekend landed in the middle. That's it. That's the whole mystery.

And even in the worst case where she *was* mildly annoyed — mildly annoyed people still pay you, they just do it while sighing. The money moves the same either way.

So: wait for Monday, check your account first thing, and only text if it's not there. Odds are this resolves itself and future-you gets to laugh about the spiral. ✨

Okay okay you talked me down haha. That... actually makes a lot of sense. I think I just needed someone to tell me it's not personal.

Alright I'll wait til Monday morning 🤓 Thanks for the pep talk!

Anytime! That's what friends are for — sometimes you just need an outside voice to say "it's paperwork, not a grudge." 😄

You've got a solid plan: check the account Monday morning, text only if needed, and keep the friendly draft in your back pocket. My money's on the deposit quietly showing up and this whole thing becoming a funny story about the time you almost made $85 into A Thing.

Good luck Monday — go enjoy your weekend, you've earned it (literally, you sat a cat for it). 🐱✨

Okay wait, one more thing haha. If I do end up texting her Monday, should I mention the wrong voided check or just leave it out completely? I feel like acknowledging it shows I'm on top of it but also like... maybe that draws attention to the mistake lol

Ooh, good instinct to think this through — but you've actually already threaded the needle without realizing it! Look at the draft I gave you:

"...just want to make sure the new check form went through okay 🙂"

That one little phrase does exactly what you want: it shows you're on top of your paperwork *and* gives her an easy way to say "yep, got it!" — but it frames the form as a logistics question, not an apology. You're not saying "sorry I messed up," you're saying "confirming the admin stuff is squared away," which reads as organized rather than guilty.

What I'd avoid is anything beyond that — no "sorry again about the wrong form!" or re-explaining what happened. Over-apologizing is what draws attention to the mistake. One casual reference = conscientious. Multiple references = you keep poking the bruise. 😄

So: send the draft as-is, and you're golden.
